_readme: Semantic vocabularies for canonical fields whose VALUE is unambiguous but whose
MEANING is not. Three of the 23 fields have this shape:
Date      a date, but which date? transaction / registration / handover / lease
Size      a number, but in what unit? sq ft / sq m
AREA      a place, but at what level? Community / Sub-Community
These are data, not code. Adding a date_type is an edit to this file plus an
ENGINE_VERSION bump -- never a code change. Order within 'types' is the tie-break
order used when two types score equally, so put the most common first.
signals.header      substrings matched against the ORIGINAL source header
signals.neighbour   canonical fields present in the same sheet that make this
signals.companion   other raw headers in the same sheet
min_confidence      below this the observation is routed to review, never guessed

types.name: transaction_date
types.description: Date the sale, transfer or procedure was executed.

types.name: registration_date
types.description: Date the plot or unit was recorded in the land registry.

types.name: handover_date
types.description: Date the unit was handed over to the owner.

types.name: lease_end_date
types.description: Date a tenancy ends or expires.

types.name: listing_date
types.description: Date the property was listed, or the contact enquired.

types.name: sqft
types.description: Area in square feet. The UAE market default.

types.name: sqm
types.description: Area in square metres. Converted to sq ft on write; a mis-read here is a 10.76x error.

AREA._note: Not a canonical field. The raw header 'AREA' (685 occurrences) is the largest ambiguous label in the corpus: header_mapping_completed.xlsx reads it as Community, header_mapping_completed_updated.xlsx as Sub-Community. Resolved per source file from sample values -- see ADR-003.

types.name: community
types.description: Master community. Resolves when AREA's values match known Community vocabulary and no separate Community column exists.

types.name: sub_community
types.description: Area or sector within a master community.
